newsitem.title: CHINA: HK's Airport Authority to set HK$3.0 bln loan.
newsitem.headline: HK's Airport Authority to set HK$3.0 bln loan.

text.p: Hong Kong's Airport Authority (AA) said on Tuesday it had mandated four banks to arrange a three-year HK$3.0 billion revolving credit facility.
The four banks are China Development Finance Co (Hong Kong) Ltd, Tokyo-Mitsubishi International (HK), Chase Manhattan Asia Ltd and HSBC Investment Bank Asia.
CDFC and Chase Manhattan Bank are the bookrunners.
The AA said the facility will pay a margin of 30 basis points per annum plus fees, which have not been disclosed.
General syndication will begin after sub-underwriting by the co-arrangers has been completed, with a view to signing the credit agreement by September 15, 1997.

Proceeds of the facility will be used for general corporate purposes, including financing a second runway and a concourse at Hong Kong's new Chek Lap Kok airport as well as for new capital expenditures.
The Authority said the new facility will not be used to finance the opening phase of the airport, known as Phase 1a, for which sufficient funding has been arranged.
In January 1996, the Authority signed a credit agreement with 48 banks for a five-year facility of HK$8.2 billion to finance Phase 1a of the airport project.
Loans drawn under that facility will be repaid in full by September 30, 2001.
Barring unforeseen circumstances, the Authority expects that facility to be sufficient for Phase 1a, and drawdown will commence in October this year.
Separate arrangements for an Airport Authority Note Issuance Programme to be arranged by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority also have been completed, subject to execution of legal documents.
With this programme, the Authority will be able to issue fixed or floating rate paper with a maturity of up to 10 years.
